title: The Ground Under You Is Moving Right Now! 🌍
description: Earth's crust is split into giant plates that move every year! See how stress builds up between them and suddenly releases as an earthquake — and why each magnitude step is so much stronger.

scenes.say: The ground you're standing on is moving right now, and you can't feel it. But sometimes it moves suddenly… and that's an earthquake.

scenes.caption: Tectonic plates
scenes.say: Earth's crust isn't one piece. It's split into giant slabs called tectonic plates, floating on hot, slowly flowing rock.

scenes.label: About as fast as your nails grow
scenes.say: These plates move two to ten centimeters a year, roughly as fast as your fingernails grow.
Where two plates grind past each other, they get stuck and stress builds for years. Then the rock suddenly slips, releasing energy as waves that shake the ground.

scenes.text: Each step up means about 32 times more energy
scenes.say: Did you know a magnitude seven quake isn't just a bit stronger than a six? It releases about thirty-two times more energy!
